question: Usually, which year of a series of years in an economic index is called the base year?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**First Year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A base year is the** first of a series of years **in an economic or financial index.
 
• New,** up-to-date base years are periodically introduced** to keep data current in a particular index.
 
• **Any year can serve as a base year,** but analysts typically choose recent years.
 
• Base year re**fers to the base point in the time of a time series.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Economic Index is a **statistical measure of change in a representative group of individual data points.**
 
• These data may be derived from **any number of sources, including company performance, prices, productivity, and employment**.
